candidates.title: Live-work-farm hybrid housing program
candidates.shift: A single-site building program splits into 10% residence, 40% pig farm, 50% sustainable agriculture — blending dwelling and food production into one real-estate parcel.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could presage zoning/design categories for integrated agri-residential real estate in peripheral markets; strange because mainstream retail/real estate rarely designs for livestock adjacency.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily project brief describing PIN'N PAN House's program split across residence, pig farming, and agriculture.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of blending domestic and productive land use at building scale; if it spreads, zoning and real-estate typologies could evolve to formally mix dwelling, retail, and food production, especially in resilience-focused rural/peripheral markets.
candidates.author: Pratik Mour

candidates.title: Inflatable rolling robot for extreme-terrain exploration
candidates.shift: A 1.8m inflatable ball robot designed for lunar terrain is being tested on rugged earthly quarry ground, suggesting terrestrial extreme-environment applications.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative, off-map (space robotics) but could eventually touch construction/infrastructure inspection in hazardous sites — mines, disaster zones, or post-collapse retail/industrial structures.
candidates.evidence: IEEE Spectrum report on a 150kg inflatable robot tested in a Texas quarry as a lunar-terrain analog.
candidates.initial_analysis: Robotics built for unstructured, unpredictable terrain; if adapted terrestrially, could enable hazardous-site inspection/rehabilitation of damaged buildings or industrial sites without human risk — an off-map (space) technology with a plausible construction-safety path.
candidates.author: Max G. Levy

candidates.title: Behavior-first reframing of market retrofit
candidates.shift: A study argues traditional-market revitalization fails when physical upgrades (roofs, façades) ignore everyday trading routines — reframing 'revitalization' from cosmetic to behavioral-spatial fit.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: retail retrofit success criteria shift from visible aesthetics to fit with informal operational behavior; could apply to Western dead-mall/store retrofits too.
candidates.evidence: Archvisual Jurnal study of Tanjung Raja Market, Indonesia, on behavioral-spatial diagnosis of market revitalization outcomes.
candidates.initial_analysis: Reframes retail-space renewal success from aesthetics to ethnographic fit with trading behavior; if adopted, retrofit programs for stores/markets would prioritize behavioral study before capital renovation, a possible template for adaptive reuse of struggling retail formats.
candidates.author: Wienty Triyuly, Aulyandini Amalia Zahra Putri, Abdurrachman Arief

candidates.title: Contaminated industrial site reborn as public art park
candidates.shift: A remediated brownfield site becomes a public park anchored by an art installation, framed under a 'waste to promise' philosophy blending remediation, art, and climate science.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could model reuse of obsolete/contaminated retail-adjacent industrial land (dead malls, former big-box sites) as hybrid civic-cultural assets rather than pure demolition/redevelopment.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of Crystal Sauna at the WasteLand park, built on a remediated industrial site in Skellefteå.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from treating industrial brownfields as pure liability toward civic/cultural asset conversion; if scaled, could inform redevelopment strategy for obsolete retail/industrial real estate that combines remediation cost with placemaking value.
candidates.author: Cristina Popescu
